messages.subject: summarise &  numcolwise
parts:
Hi,

i want a summary for a data.frame with several hundred "numeric"
columns
but struggle a bit with summarise and numcolwise.

Thanks for any advice

#### This works fine , but i have no .id attribute and my own function
#####
ddply(iris, .(Species), numcolwise(mean), na.rm = T)


df.result <- ddply(iris,summarise,numcolwise(mysummary))


mysummary <- function(x) {
print(str(x))
count=length(x)
count0=length(x[x>0])
pct0=ifelse(count0 > 0,round(count0/count,4),0)
min=min(x,na.rm=TRUE)
max=max(x,na.rm=TRUE)
mean=round(mean(x,na.rm=TRUE),4)
median=median(x,na.rm=TRUE)
sd=round(sd(x,na.rm=TRUE),4)
unique=unique(x)
return(cbind(count,count0,pct0,min,max,mean,median,sd,unique))
}

messages.subject: Re: summarise & numcolwise
parts:
Hi:

The trick in ddply() is that usually you want to supply a data frame
as input and return a data frame as output. I made the following
changes in mysummary(): (i) I took out the print() statement and the
vector of unique values; (ii) I made the input argument a data frame
(which will be reshaped, as you'll see below) and defined x as the
'value' variable of the input data frame; (iii) I returned a data
frame as output.

mysummary <- function(d) { # d is a data frame
# print(str(x))
x <- d$value

count=length(x)
count0=length(x[x>0])
pct0=ifelse(count0 > 0,round(count0/count,4),0)
min=min(x,na.rm=TRUE)
max=max(x,na.rm=TRUE)
mean=round(mean(x,na.rm=TRUE),4)
median=median(x,na.rm=TRUE)
sd=round(sd(x,na.rm=TRUE),4)

# unique=unique(x)
data.frame(count = count, count0 = count0, pct0 = pct0,
min = min, max = max, mean = mean, median = median, sd = sd)
}

# Next, I melted the data so that the variables became a factor named
'variable' with a corresponding variable name 'value':

library(plyr)
library(reshape)
u <- melt(iris, id = 'Species')
names(u)

> ddply(u, .(variable), mysummary)
variable count count0 pct0 min max mean median sd
1 Sepal.Length 150 150 1 4.3 7.9 5.8433 5.80 0.8281
2 Sepal.Width 150 150 1 2.0 4.4 3.0573 3.00 0.4359
3 Petal.Length 150 150 1 1.0 6.9 3.7580 4.35 1.7653
4 Petal.Width 150 150 1 0.1 2.5 1.1993 1.30 0.7622

The problem with using unique(x) in your function is that it will
return a vector that will not necessarily have the same length from
one variable to the next; especially in columnwise(), that's not going
to work. You could try to put it back in and rerun it with the melted
data frame; there's a possibility that would work, but all the summary
values would be duplicated in the process for each variable.

columnwise() can be pretty touchy, so in this case it's better to
reshape the data frame and use the variables as a factor over which
mysummary() can be applied.

HTH,
Dennis
